task: Face detection. Graded two ways on real frames: recall - every face a human can see must be found, and its box must agree with the platform's own already-`production` face detector (insightface-buffalo-l-detect / SCRFD) at IoU >= 0.5 on the same frame; and false positives - frames with no human face in them at all must return zero detections.

tolerance.note: IoU is measured against SCRFD's own box, not a hand-drawn ground truth: SCRFD is already `production` in this registry and independently validated, so it is the best real reference available here, and two detectors from unrelated architecture families agreeing on a box location is meaningful evidence that both decoded the frame correctly. It is NOT a claim that SCRFD's box is pixel-perfect truth - IoU 0.5 is deliberately a loose 'same face, same place' bar rather than a tight one, because RetinaFace and SCRFD genuinely use slightly different box conventions around the chin/hairline.

note: Only one real, usable source image exists anywhere in this repo's committed fixtures with clearly visible human faces - stock_streetscene_3adults.jpg (already used by intern-child-adult-detection and the other uniface golden sets). A third person in that photo is cropped at the frame edge and is not detected by SCRFD either, so only the 2 fully-visible faces are listed as expected. The three Autotek frames are real customer-site NVR captures with no human face at any usable resolution - they are the negative controls, and they are what makes the false-positive rate a real measurement rather than an untested zero.

faces.note: Younger man, dark jacket/red top, dark square sunglasses.
Bearded man, tan coat, round amber sunglasses.

images.note: Real Autotek NVR frame, interior storage room, no people.
Real Autotek NVR frame, garage with parked vehicles, no people.
Real Autotek NVR frame, night IR, effectively blank. Also the only night/IR condition anywhere in this set - see CLAUDE.md on night detection thresholds being unvalidated generally.

unmeasured: Landmark ACCURACY. The 5 points are structurally correct (right count, right order, and on the real faces they land within ~1-2px of SCRFD's own 5 points), but no hand-labelled 5-point ground truth exists in this repo, so landmark error is not scored anywhere in this manifest.
Night/IR recall. The one night frame here is a negative control - it contains no face, so it tests false positives only. No real face has ever been tested against this model under IR.
Crowded / small-face / rotated-face recall. Two upright, unoccluded (bar sunglasses) adult faces in one photo is the entire positive set.
